commentary: Today, Dalian iron ore futures opened higher and conƟnued to rise, reaching a peak of 833 yuan/mt before slightly retreaƟng. The most-traded contract I2501 ﬂuctuated upward throughout the day and ﬁnally closed at 817 yuan/mt, up 1.87% for the day. Traders were acƟvely selling, while steel mills remained cauƟous with moderate purchase willingness. Market transacƟons were relaƟvely few today. In Shandong, the mainstream transacƟon prices for PB ﬁnes were 795-800 yuan/mt, up 5 yuan/mt from yesterday; in Tangshan, the transacƟon prices for PB ﬁnes were 810-815 yuan/mt, up 5- 10 yuan/mt from yesterday. Yesterday's Politburo meeƟng released several posiƟve signals, indicaƟng that future monetary and ﬁscal policies will be relaƟvely loose, which signiﬁcantly boosted market senƟment. However, according to SMM's survey on blast furnace maintenance, due to environmental protecƟon-driven producƟon restricƟons in Hebei, many steel mills were forced to shut down and maintain their blast furnaces. The impact from maintenance increased by more than 200,000 mt WoW. This weakened the demand for iron ore, limiƟng the rise in ore prices. Nevertheless, considering the upcoming economic conference, market senƟment remains opƟmisƟc, and ore prices are expected to maintain a ﬂuctuaƟng upward trend in the short term.
